$comment: The owner's routing decision for the build server (policy build-server-routes-all-ci; Doc/Architecture/BuildHosts → "Host-forced routing"). Every repository named in hostForced has its PULL-REQUEST CI routed to the standing build host even while its .github/build-stages.json still owes parity (no "ciEquivalent": true): build-executor.py answers `host-forced` = SHADOW until parity: the run is queued on the host (its own check runs show its real result, none required) while every lane runs its legs on GitHub Actions exactly as with `actions`, and those carry the required verdict; the owed gap is printed as warnings, never a red. Read from core's DEFAULT branch only (build-executor.py ROUTING_URL), so no pull request routes itself. It narrows nothing on its own: the operations instance must ALSO answer host for the repository (Hosting:Builds:HostRepos). Trunk runs are never forced. A repository leaves this list when its stages claim equivalence (then it routes as plain `host`) or when the owner reverses the decision. MeshWeaver.Deploy and Memex are deliberately absent: they carry the host's fixes and the infrastructure and must stay mergeable.
